To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inter-Korean economic relations during the 2002-2006 period were not affected by the military conflict and the nuclear crisis, because the South Korean business actors were motivated by economic gain, and the North Korean counterpart was not able to impose any economic pressure on South Korean traders due to its economic weakness.

South Korean entrepreneurs continued trade with their North Korean partners despite the nuclear crisis, which was caused by the North Korean nuclear development, because they could gain economic benefits from the trade relationship with the North.
the South Korean traders were motivated by their economic needs to continue their trade with North Korea despite the rising military tensions caused by the North Korea's nuclear development.
